message.reasoning_content:
a.txt: 17, -4, 23, 8 → 44.
b.txt words: pear, apple, pear, plum, Apple, apple, fig, plum → unique case-sensitive: pear, apple, plum, Apple, fig → sorted by dictionary order (case-sensitive, so uppercase before lowercase in ASCII): "Apple", "apple", "fig", "pear", "plum" → 5 words.

Now write outputs. Use shell commands for real computation (awk/sort) rather than hardcoding, to be honest.

Create out dir and compute.

function.name: shell
function.arguments:
{"command": "mkdir -p out
awk '{s+=$1} END{print s}' data/a.txt > out/sum.txt
tr -s '[:space:]' '\n' < data/b.txt | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u > out/words.txt
echo "sum=$(cat out/sum.txt)"
echo "words=$(wc -l < out/words.txt)"
cat out/words.txt"}
